previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient, a male with a history of alcoholic cirrhosis, hepatitis C, and esophageal varices, was admitted for evaluation of hematemesis and melena. Initial workup revealed a drop in hemoglobin from baseline, leading to concern for upper gastrointestinal bleeding. He was started on octreotide, pantoprazole, and ceftriaxone, and underwent an endoscopy which showed no active bleeding but confirmed grade one esophageal varices. A urinary tract infection due to Enterococcus was identified and treated with a seven-day course of amoxicillin. Due to a history of positive syphilis serology and behavioral concerns, a lumbar puncture was performed; cerebrospinal fluid analysis showed no signs of neurosyphilis, though confirmatory results remained pending at discharge. The patient was monitored for alcohol withdrawal using the CIWA scale but did not require treatment. He was discharged home with instructions to complete antibiotics, undergo a repeat endoscopy in eight weeks, and follow up with his primary care and liver specialists. Medication adjustments included holding lisinopril and furosemide, switching nadolol to bedtime dosing, and adding folic acid.

Brief Hospital Course:
Mr. ___ is a ___ year old man with a history of Hepatitis C & 
alcoholic cirrhosis, varices, and gastritis who presented to the 
ED intoxicated with a complaint of bloody stools, found to have 
a bleeding AVM on EGD. Mr. ___ left the hospital against 
medical advice. 

ACTIVE ISSUES:
#  Upper Gastrointestinal Bleed: 
Mr. ___ presented with a complaint of hematemesis and bloody 
stools. He required a central line for venous access. He was 
transfused 1 unit pRBCs. He had no further episodes of bleeding 
and his hemoglobin was stable throughout the hospitalization. 
EGD revealed a small oozing AVM noted in the antrum which was 
treated with APC to achieve hemostasis. He received ceftriaxone 
for infection prophylaxis, was treated with a PPI drip, and 
discharged on an oral PPI. Mr. ___ left the hospital against 
medical advice while a follow up CBC was pending. 

# Abdominal pain: Mr. ___ complained of abdominal pain. He 
had no peritoneal signs on abdominal exam. Abdominal ultrasound 
showed no ascites, no portal vein thrombosis, and no mass within 
the liver. His pain was treated with Tramadol. 
  
# Hypertension: He presented hypertensive with systolic blood 
pressure as high as the 180s. His lisinopril, which had been 
held at previous admission was restarted. Nadolol was held 
initially but was restarted after he remained hemodynamically 
stable. His blood pressure was controlled in the 140s at the 
time of discharge. 

# Alcohol Abuse - He presented intoxicated. He was kept on a 
CIWA scale on which he initially scored a 6 but ultimately 
trended to 0. He required no benzodiazepines for withdrawal. 

CHRONIC/INACTIVE ISSUES:
# Cirrhosis: Due to alcohol abuse and hepatitis C. MELD at 
presentation was 12 although he is not on the transplant list 
given his active drinking. He had mild asterixis at ___ 
but was not overtly encephalopathic and this resolved asterixis 
by discharge. Infectious workup was unremarkable. EGD showed 
grade I-II varices and he continued nadolol.
